title: fix(sse): streaming chunking/framing fixes for partial JSON, delimiter ordering, and token/event ordering
author: Evan Chen
description:
Context: Several production incidents and downstream client reports indicated intermittent JSON parse errors and truncated objects when clients consumed SSE streams from the OpenAI-compat and native /stream endpoints. Root cause analysis identified three related issues: 1) the SSE framing logic could emit data event fragments that split JSON tokens mid-codepoint when UTF-8 multibyte sequences were present, 2) delimiter ordering between 'data:' prefixes and blank-line event terminators was not consistently preserved under high-concurrency batching, and 3) the encoder sometimes reordered token emission relative to event boundaries when KV cache flushes and batching coalescing occurred. This PR fixes the framing and chunking state machine to guarantee that partial JSON fragments are emitted on event boundaries only and that delimiter ordering follows the SSE spec expectations.

What I changed (summary):
- Introduced a streaming Framer in runtime/sse/framer.go that tracks UTF-8 safe boundaries and JSON token boundaries to avoid splitting multi-byte codepoints or JSON tokens across SSE data fragments.
- Ensured all emitted SSE events follow the exact ordering: write 'data: ' fragment(s) -> newline -> (additional 'data: ' lines when multi-line) -> newline blank-line terminator. This removes races where blank-line terminators could be sent before pending data was fully flushed.
- Added a sequence_id header on events only as a compatibility fallback for older clients that could not reconstruct ordering; the main fix relies on proper framing but sequence_id helps debugging and rollbacks.
- Adjusted the batching/coalescing logic in runtime/serve/streaming_dispatcher.go to flush outstanding token buffers before triggering an event boundary caused by KV cache eviction or resharding.
- Fixed a bug in the OpenAI-compat shim (openai_compat/stream_encoder.py) where the shim attempted to re-chunk already-framed SSE payloads, which resulted in double-framing and delimiter inversion when combined with native framer backpressure.
- Added comprehensive unit and integration tests: runtime/sse/framer_test.go, openai_compat/stream_encoder_test.py, and a new e2e streaming integration that fuzzes UTF-8 boundaries and ensures valid JSON is reconstructable by the client.

- 51234b: fix dispatcher flush points and integrate framer

- runtime/sse/framer_test.go (new)

- integrations/e2e/streaming_fuzz.py (new)

Why this approach: The safest way to resolve downstream JSON parse errors is to avoid emitting partial bytes that break UTF-8 or JSON token boundaries. Rather than adding brittle heuristics in multiple places, a small, focused Framer centralizes the logic and provides clear semantics for downstream shims (OpenAI compat) and the dispatcher. Sequence ids are optional and only included to aid debugging during rollout.

Testing and CI: Local unit tests and the new fuzz integration were run repeatedly. CI details: initial CI run showed an intermittent integration failure in "integration-sse" caused by a timing assumption in the test harness; I adjusted the harness to wait for event terminators and re-ran. Final CI summary: unit-tests: pass, lint: pass, integration-sse: pass (after rerun), e2e-streaming-fuzz: pass. See ci_checks for per-check notes.

Rollout plan: Gradual rollout behind a feature flag 'sse_framer_v1' for 48 hours in staging, then enable for 10% of traffic in prod for 24 hours with automated alerting on client JSON parse errors and increase to 100% if no regressions. The OpenAI-compat shim change is backward-compatible; if issues arise, the feature flag can be toggled and sequence_id will help reconstruct partial events.

Backwards compatibility and migration: No breaking API changes. This is a bug fix that tightens framing semantics; clients that incorrectly depended on previous delimiter races should see improved behavior. The OpenAI-compat layer continues to advertise the same streaming contract.

Checklist:
- [x] Unit tests
- [x] Integration tests
- [x] E2E fuzz tests for UTF-8 and JSON token boundaries
- [x] Docs update
- [x] Added feature-flag gating for rollout

Notes for reviewers: Pay attention to framer.go correctness around rune boundaries and the JSON token scan window (I added comments explaining the algorithm). I specifically request review of the dispatcher flush points (L120-L185 in streaming_dispatcher.go) because aggressive flushes caused previous regressions.

release_notes: Fix: SSE streaming framing now avoids splitting UTF-8 and JSON tokens across data fragments; resolves intermittent client JSON parse errors and improves streaming stability for OpenAI-compat endpoints.
notes: Hotfix candidate: if customer impact observed, toggle 'sse_framer_v1' feature flag to roll back quickly. Sequence ids can be used to reconcile out-of-order reconstructed events if necessary.
